mainTopic: Forbidden sights and their limits, מלאך המות, the ladder of spiritual traits, and selling attached produce or animals to a גוי on condition
overview: This amud finishes a ברייתא listing things a person must not gaze at, including a woman's colored clothes and animals while they mate. It then tells how מלאך המות, who is full of eyes, kills with a drop of poison. The גמרא answers the question about רבן גמליאל: he saw the woman by surprise at a corner. It then limits the ban on a woman's clothes. רב פפא says it applies only if you know the owner, and רב חסדא says it applies only to clothes she has worn; the proof for רב חסדא is turned back. The גמרא explains more lines of the מלאך המות ברייתא, then brings רבי פנחס בן יאיר's ladder of spiritual growth, and רבי יהושע בן לוי, who says humility is the greatest trait. Back on the law, רבי יהודה and רבי מאיר argue about selling a tree, fodder, grain, or an animal to a גוי on condition that he cuts or slaughters it. A new משנה then begins about renting houses and fields to a גוי, and that משנה continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The rest of the list of forbidden sights
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends its list: a person must not gaze at a woman's colored clothes or at animals while they mate, even if he were full of eyes like מלאך המות.
steps.simpleTranslation: And one may not look at a woman's colored garments, or at a male or female donkey, a male or female pig, or birds while they are mating. This holds even if a person were full of eyes like the Angel of Death.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a quote from a ברייתא that lists things a person must avoid looking at. This ברייתא is the source being used to challenge the story of רבן גמליאל, who looked at a beautiful woman.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא adds two items: a woman's colored clothing and animals while they mate. The last phrase means no excuse helps here. Even someone who sees in every direction may not look on purpose.

phrases.english: and not at the colored garments of a woman,
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets, 'of,' is added in the corrected wording. Later, רבא quotes the line without it.

phrases.english: and not at a male donkey or a female donkey,
and not at a male pig or a female pig,
and not at birds
at the time when they are mating with each other,
phrases.notes: This applies to all the animals just listed, not only to the birds.

phrases.english: and even if one were full of eyes like the Angel of Death.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא quoted earlier on the daf as a challenge to רבן גמליאל's looking at a woman.
steps.kashyaTarget: The story that רבן גמליאל looked at a beautiful woman
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא forbids gazing at attractive or immodest sights, so how could רבן גמליאל look?

steps.title: How the Angel of Death takes a life
steps.stepSummary: Prompted by the phrase 'full of eyes,' the גמרא describes מלאך המות and how a sick person dies.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said that the Angel of Death is completely full of eyes. When a sick person is about to die, he stands above the person's head with his sword drawn. A drop of poison hangs from the sword. When the sick person sees him, he trembles and opens his mouth, and the angel throws the drop in. From that drop he dies, from it his body rots, and from it his face turns greenish.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a side story. The ברייתא just mentioned מלאך המות being 'full of eyes,' so the גמרא explains who that is and what he does.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is אגדה, not a legal step. It explains the phrase from the ברייתא and does not move the argument about looking forward. After it, the גמרא goes back to the question about רבן גמליאל.

phrases.english: They said about him, about the Angel of Death,
that he is entirely full of eyes,
at the time a sick person is passing away
he stands above his head,
with his sword drawn in his hand,
and a drop of poison hanging on it,
phrases.notes: 'On it' means on the sword.

phrases.english: once the sick person sees him,
he trembles and opens his mouth,
and he throws it into his mouth,
from it he dies, from it he rots,
from it his face turns green!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the phrase 'full of eyes like the Angel of Death' from the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מלאך המות is full of eyes and kills the sick person with a drop of poison from his sword.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל saw her by surprise at a corner
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the challenge: רבן גמליאל did not look on purpose. He came around a corner and saw the woman suddenly.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was a corner. He turned a corner and saw her without planning to.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now goes back to the question and answers it. רבן גמליאל saw the woman by accident when they met at a corner.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא forbids staring on purpose. It does not forbid an unplanned glance. Since רבן גמליאל saw her suddenly at a corner, his story does not contradict the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: a corner, where two paths meet

steps.whatToRemember: The ban is on looking on purpose. An accidental, unplanned sight, like meeting someone around a corner, is not included.

phrases.english: It was a corner.
phrases.notes: He means רבן גמליאל came around a corner and saw her before he could avoid it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns from the side story to answer the challenge raised by the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the case: it was an accidental sight, not purposeful gazing
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבן גמליאל looked at the woman on purpose, against the ברייתא.
steps.terutzMaskana: He saw her suddenly at a corner, which the ברייתא does not forbid.

steps.title: Even garments spread on a wall
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the ברייתא's line about a woman's colored clothes. שמואל says the ban applies even when the clothes are spread on a wall.
steps.simpleTranslation: About the line 'nor at the colored garments of a woman': רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל that this applies even when they are spread out on a wall.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא picks one line from the ברייתא and explains it. שמואל says the rule covers clothes that are not being worn.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might think the rule applies only while a woman wears the clothes. שמואל widens it: the clothes alone, hanging on a wall, are also included. Looking at them can lead to thinking about the woman.

phrases.english: Nor at the colored garments of a woman.
Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
Even when they are spread on a wall.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֹא בְּבִגְדֵי צֶבַע [שֶׁל] אִשָּׁה. אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to one line of the ברייתא from step 1 to explain it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ban on gazing at a woman's colored garments applies even when they are not being worn.

steps.title: Only when you know whose clothes they are
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא limits the rule: it applies only when the person knows who owns the clothes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: And this is only when he knows their owner.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא adds a limit to the rule about colored clothes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry is that the clothes will make him think about the woman. That happens only if he knows who she is. If he does not know the owner, there is no ban.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
And only when he knows their owner.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the rule that שמואל stated.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ban applies only when one knows the woman who owns the garments.

steps.title: The wording of the ברייתא supports רב פפא
steps.stepSummary: רבא proves רב פפא's limit from the wording: the ברייתא says 'a woman's colored garments,' not just 'colored garments.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The wording is exact too. It says 'nor at the colored garments of a woman,' and not 'nor at colored garments.' Learn from this that the rule is about a woman he knows.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא brings support for רב פפא from the exact words of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If any colored clothing were forbidden, the ברייתא could have said simply 'colored garments.' Mentioning 'a woman' points to a specific woman, so the ban is when he knows her. This backs up רב פפא's limit, and רב חסדא adds one more limit in the next step.
steps.whatToRemember: A woman's colored garments may not be gazed at, even when they hang on a wall. This applies only when he knows the woman they belong to.

phrases.english: Rava said: The wording is also precise,
since it teaches 'nor at the colored garments of a woman,'
and it does not teach 'nor at colored garments,'
learn from it.
phrases.notes: He means: learn that the rule is about the clothes of a woman he knows.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב פפא's limit from the wording of the ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: רב פפא's rule that the ban applies only when he knows the owner
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's words 'garments of a woman' rather than simply 'colored garments'

steps.title: The ban applies only to old, worn clothes
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא limits the ban: it covers only old clothes a woman has worn, not new ones.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: This rule is only about old clothes. With new clothes, there is no problem.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא adds another limit to the rule against looking at a woman's colored clothes. The ban applies only to clothes she has already worn.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 4-6 said the ban applies even to clothes spread on a wall, but only if you know who owns them. רב חסדא narrows it more. New clothes have never been worn by the woman, so looking at them leads to no improper thoughts.

keyTerms.meaning: This rule applies only to... (a limiting phrase)
Old garments, ones that have been worn
We have no problem with it; it is allowed

phrases.english: Rav Ḥisda said:
This applies only to old garments,
phrases.notes: "This" is the ban on looking at a woman's colored clothes, from the steps just before.

phrases.english: but with new ones, we have no problem with it,

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: הָנֵי מִילֵּי בְּעַתִּיקֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another limit on שמואל's rule, after רב פפא's limit and רבא's proof.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ban on looking at a woman's colored garments applies only to worn (old) garments, not to new ones.

steps.title: Proof from giving clothes to a launderer
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא proves his limit: otherwise, how could anyone give a woman's new garment to a launderer, who has to look at it?
steps.simpleTranslation: For if you don't say this, how could we ever give a garment to a launderer? He looks at it!
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא brings a proof for his limit from everyday practice. People send new garments to a launderer, and nobody objects.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The launderer has to look closely at the clothes he works on. If looking at new women's clothes were forbidden, sending clothes to him would be a problem. Since this is normal and accepted, new clothes must be allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: For if you do not say so (introduces a proof)
A launderer, one who prepares new cloth for use

phrases.english: for if you do not say so,
how could we give a garment to a launderer?
But he is looking at it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב חסדא's limit from step 7.
steps.raayaObject: רב חסדא's rule that new garments are permitted to look at.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The accepted practice of giving new garments to a launderer, who must look at them.

steps.title: The launderer is different: he is busy with his work
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the launderer proof using רב יהודה's rule about mating animals. Someone busy with his work does not come to bad thoughts.
steps.simpleTranslation: But by your logic, what about רב יהודה's rule that a person may put one animal into another of its own kind, like a brush into a tube? He is looking too! The answer must be that he is busy with his work. The launderer is also busy with his work.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רב חסדא's proof. A launderer cannot teach us about regular people, because he is focused on his job.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה lets a person help animals mate even though he sees it, because he is busy working. The same applies to a launderer, so his case proves nothing about new clothes. רב חסדא's rule itself is not rejected. Only his proof falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: And according to your reasoning (turns the argument back on the speaker)
One species with its own species
Like a brush into a tube (a kohl brush into its holder)
He is busy with his work

steps.confusionAlert: This step does not cancel רב חסדא's rule about new clothes. It only shows that the launderer case is not a good proof for it.

phrases.english: And according to your reasoning,
what about that which Rav Yehuda said:
one species with its own species, it is permitted to insert
phrases.notes: He means guiding a male animal into a female of the same kind when they mate.

phrases.english: like a brush into a tube,
but he is looking!
Rather, he is busy with his work;
so too, he is busy with his work.
phrases.notes: This second "he" is the launderer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 8.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the launderer proof is rejected; רב חסדא's limit about new clothes stays standing.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A launderer is busy with his work and will not have improper thoughts, so his case says nothing about ordinary people looking at new clothes.

steps.title: Does 'he dies from the drop' argue with אבוה דשמואל?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the ברייתא: the sick person dies from the drop on the angel's sword. That seems to clash with אבוה דשמואל, who heard that מלאך המות slaughters people.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא said: from that drop he dies. Shall we say this argues with אבוה דשמואל? He said: The Angel of Death told me, 'If I were not worried about people's dignity, I would open up the place of slaughter like an animal's.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the ברייתא from step 2 about מלאך המות. It points out a possible contradiction between two descriptions of how a person dies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says death comes from a drop that falls into the person's mouth. אבוה דשמואל suggests the angel actually slaughters people like an animal, cutting the throat. Those sound like two different ways of dying.

phrases.english: The Master said: From it he dies.
phrases.notes: "It" is the drop on the sword of מלאך המות, from the ברייתא in step 2.

phrases.english: Shall we say this disagrees with Shmuel's father?
For Shmuel's father said:
The Angel of Death said to me:
"If I were not concerned for the dignity of people,
I would uncover the place of slaughter, like an animal's."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר: מִמֶּנָּה מֵת. נֵימָא פְּלִיגָא דַּאֲבוּהּ דִּשְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of looking at clothes and returns to the ברייתא about מלאך המות.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's statement that a person dies from the drop.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: אבוה דשמואל suggests death comes by slaughter, not by a drop, so the two sources seem to argue.

steps.title: The drop itself cuts the throat
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers: maybe the drop is what cuts the סימנים, so both descriptions are true.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps that drop is what cuts the סימנים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the contradiction. The drop and the slaughter are really one event.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The drop works by cutting the windpipe and food pipe, the way a שחיטה does. So the ברייתא (death from the drop) and אבוה דשמואל (death like slaughter) fit together.

keyTerms.meaning: The two organs cut in שחיטה: the windpipe and the food pipe

phrases.english: Perhaps that drop
cuts the simanim.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Harmonization: both sources describe the same event.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Death from a drop and death by slaughter are two different ways of dying.
steps.terutzMaskana: The drop itself cuts the סימנים, so it is a kind of slaughter.

steps.title: 'From it he decays' supports turning the dead onto his face
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says the body decays from the drop. That supports the teaching from בי רב: to keep a body from decaying, turn it onto its face.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא said: from that drop the body decays. This supports רבי חנינא בר כהנא, who said that they taught in the school of רב: Whoever wants his dead relative not to decay should turn him onto his face.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא looks at the next line of the ברייתא and shows that it supports a practical teaching from the school of רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The drop entered through the mouth, and the ברייתא says it causes decay. That explains why turning the body face-down helps slow the decay. So the ברייתא backs up the advice of בי רב.

keyTerms.meaning: He should turn him onto his face

steps.whatToRemember: The ban on looking at a woman's clothes applies only to worn clothes. A launderer is a weak proof, because he is busy with his work. The drop from מלאך המות's sword kills by cutting the סימנים, and it also causes the body to decay.

phrases.english: From it he decays.

phrases.aramaic: מְסַיַּיע לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי חֲנִינָא בַּר כָּהֲנָא,
phrases.english: This supports Rabbi Ḥanina bar Kahana,
for Rabbi Ḥanina bar Kahana said:
They say in the school of Rav:
One who wants his dead relative not to decay
should turn him onto his face.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִמֶּנָּה מַסְרִיחַ. מְסַיַּיע לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי חֲנִינָא בַּר כָּהֲנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues with the next line of the same ברייתא about מלאך המות.
steps.raayaObject: The teaching of בי רב (quoted by רבי חנינא בר כהנא) to turn a dead body onto its face.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's statement that the body decays from the drop.

steps.title: Guard your thoughts by day so you do not become impure at night
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא reads the פסוק 'guard yourself from every evil thing' as a warning not to think improper thoughts by day, which can lead to impurity at night.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: 'And you shall guard yourself from every evil thing.' This means a person should not think improper thoughts during the day and then become impure at night.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another source that explains the פסוק it has been using. This ברייתא reads the פסוק as a warning about one's thoughts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The next פסוק in the תורה talks about someone who became impure from 'what happened at night.' So the ברייתא reads 'every evil thing' as the daytime thoughts that cause this. The danger starts in the mind during the day.

keyTerms.meaning: Think, let the mind dwell on improper thoughts

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: 'And you shall guard yourself from every evil thing,'
phrases.notes: דברים 23:10

phrases.english: that a person should not think improper thoughts by day
and come to impurity at night.
phrases.notes: The very next פסוק talks about a man who became impure from something that happened at night.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new ברייתא that explains the same פסוק the earlier discussion was built on.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'Guard yourself from every evil thing' warns a person not to have improper thoughts by day that lead to impurity at night.

steps.title: The ladder of spiritual growth of רבי פנחס בן יאיר
steps.stepSummary: Starting from this פסוק, רבי פנחס בן יאיר lists a chain of traits, each leading to the next, from תורה up to תחיית המתים, and says חסידות is greatest of all.
steps.simpleTranslation: From here רבי פנחס בן יאיר said: תורה leads to carefulness, carefulness to eagerness, eagerness to cleanliness, cleanliness to separation, separation to purity, purity to piety, piety to humility, humility to fear of sin, fear of sin to holiness, holiness to רוח הקודש, and רוח הקודש to תחיית המתים. And piety is greatest of all, as it says: 'Then You spoke in a vision to Your pious ones.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי פנחס בן יאיר builds on the idea of guarding oneself and gives a step-by-step ladder of spiritual growth. He ends by saying which step is the greatest.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each trait opens the door to the next, so a person climbs one rung at a time. He proves that חסידות is greatest from a פסוק where ה׳ speaks in a vision, which is prophecy, to the 'pious ones.'

keyTerms.meaning: Separating oneself, staying away from wrong
Piety, going beyond what is required
Divine spirit, a level of inspiration from ה׳

steps.whyThisMatters: This list became a classic guide to spiritual growth, and the idea of a step-by-step climb is the backbone of later מוסר works.

phrases.aramaic: מִכָּאן אָמַר רַבִּי פִּנְחָס בֶּן יָאִיר:
phrases.english: From here Rabbi Pinchas ben Yair said:
Torah leads to carefulness,
carefulness leads to eagerness,
eagerness leads to cleanliness,
phrases.notes: He means a clean soul, free of sin.

phrases.english: cleanliness leads to separation from wrong,
separation leads to purity,
purity leads to piety,
piety leads to humility,
humility leads to fear of sin,
fear of sin leads to holiness,
holiness leads to the divine spirit,

phrases.aramaic: רוּחַ הַקּוֹדֶשׁ מְבִיאָה לִידֵי תְּחִיַּית הַמֵּתִים,
phrases.english: the divine spirit leads to the resurrection of the dead,
and piety is greater than all of them,
as it is said: 'Then You spoke in a vision to Your pious ones.'
phrases.notes: תהלים 89:20

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכָּאן אָמַר רַבִּי פִּנְחָס בֶּן יָאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds a larger teaching on the idea of guarding oneself from step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Spiritual growth climbs step by step from תורה to תחיית המתים, and חסידות is the greatest trait.

steps.title: רבי יהושע בן לוי says humility is greatest
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that רבי יהושע בן לוי disagrees. He holds ענוה is greatest, because the נביא was anointed to bring news to the 'humble,' not the 'pious.'
steps.simpleTranslation: This argues with רבי יהושע בן לוי, who said: Humility is greatest of all, as it says: 'The spirit of the Lord God is upon me, because the Lord anointed me to bring good news to the humble.' It does not say 'the pious' but 'the humble,' so you learn that humility is greatest of all.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that another אמורא argues with the last part of רבי פנחס בן יאיר's teaching. רבי יהושע בן לוי says the top trait is humility, not piety.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides prove their view from a פסוק about prophecy. רבי יהושע בן לוי stresses the word choice: the פסוק could have said 'pious' but chose 'humble,' which shows humility is the highest.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי פנחס בן יאיר says חסידות is the greatest trait; רבי יהושע בן לוי says ענוה is the greatest.
steps.confusionAlert: The argument is only about which trait is greatest. רבי יהושע בן לוי is not arguing with the whole ladder from step 14.

phrases.english: And this argues with Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi,
for Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
Humility is greater than all of them,
as it is said: 'The spirit of the Lord God is upon me

phrases.aramaic: יַעַן מָשַׁח ה׳ אֹתִי לְבַשֵּׂר עֲנָוִים״,
phrases.english: because the Lord anointed me to bring good news to the humble,'
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 61:1

phrases.english: 'The pious' is not said, but rather 'the humble,'
so you have learned that humility is greater than all of them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows a different opinion about the final claim of step 14, which trait is greatest.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Humility is the greatest of all traits, learned from the word 'humble' in ישעיהו 61:1.

steps.title: Selling a tree, fodder, or standing grain to an idolater
steps.stepSummary: Back to the משנה's ban on selling attached things. A ברייתא: רבי יהודה allows selling a tree, fodder, or standing grain on condition the buyer cuts it; רבי מאיר allows selling only what is already cut.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'One may not sell to them, etc.' The Rabbis taught: One may sell them a tree on condition that he cut it down, and he cuts it down; these are the words of רבי יהודה. רבי מאיר says: One may sell them only a tree already cut down. Fodder on condition that he cut it, and he cuts it; the words of רבי יהודה. רבי מאיר says: Only fodder already cut. Standing grain on condition that he harvest it, and he harvests it; the words of רבי יהודה. רבי מאיר says: Only grain already harvested.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה, which says one may not sell idolaters things attached to the ground. It brings a ברייתא where רבי יהודה and רבי מאיר argue about selling growing things that will be cut.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה says a sale is fine if the deal requires the buyer to cut the item right away, since it will not stay attached to the land. רבי מאיר does not rely on that condition and allows only items that are already detached at the time of sale. The same argument repeats for three cases: a tree, fodder, and standing grain.

keyTerms.meaning: Fodder: grain that has grown stalks but is not yet ripe
Standing grain, still growing in the field

steps.whyThisMatters: This opens the discussion of the הלכה of when a sale counts as selling land-attached property, which the גמרא will keep exploring.

phrases.english: 'One may not sell to them, etc.'
phrases.notes: This quotes our משנה, which forbids selling idolaters things that are attached to the ground.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: One may sell them a tree
on condition that he cut it down, and he cuts it down,
these are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: אֵין מוֹכְרִין לָהֶן אֶלָּא קְצוּצָה.
phrases.english: Rabbi Meir says: One may sell them only a tree that is already cut down.
Fodder, on condition that he cut it, and he cuts it,
phrases.notes: שחת is grain that has grown stalks but is not ripe yet, often cut for animal feed.

phrases.english: these are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: אֵין מוֹכְרִין לָהֶן אֶלָּא גְּזוּזָה.
phrases.english: Rabbi Meir says: One may sell them only fodder that is already cut.
Standing grain, on condition that he harvest it, and he harvests it,
these are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: אֵין מוֹכְרִין אֶלָּא קְצוּרָה.
phrases.english: Rabbi Meir says: One may sell only grain that is already harvested.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין מוֹכְרִין לָהֶן וְכוּ׳. תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side discussion about thoughts and traits and returns to the משנה's law about selling to idolaters.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה: one may sell attached produce on condition the buyer cuts it. רבי מאיר: only produce that is already detached may be sold.

steps.title: Why the tree case alone is not enough
steps.stepSummary: If the ברייתא had only said 'tree,' we might think רבי מאיר is strict only there. A gentile loses nothing by leaving a tree in the ground, but he would lose by leaving grain in the ground.
steps.simpleTranslation: All three cases are needed. If we were only taught about a tree, we would say רבי מאיר is strict there because the gentile loses nothing by leaving it in the ground. But with something that spoils if left in the ground, we might say רבי מאיר agrees with רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a צריכותא. It is showing why the ברייתא had to mention more than one case. This first part looks at what we would have thought if only the tree were mentioned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר is afraid the gentile will not really cut what he bought. With a tree, that fear is strong, because the gentile loses nothing by leaving it standing. With standing grain, the gentile would lose by leaving it, so we might have thought רבי מאיר trusts that he will cut it.

keyTerms.meaning: It is necessary. This opens a צריכותא, which explains why every case had to be stated.
It taught us (if the text had only told us...)
He keeps it or leaves it there (in the ground)

steps.confusionAlert: A צריכותא is not a new argument about the הלכה. It only explains why the ברייתא lists several cases that seem to repeat each other.

phrases.english: And it is necessary: for if it had taught us only a tree,
in this case רבי מאיר says it must be cut first,
since he does not lose out, he will leave it standing,
phrases.notes: 'He' is the gentile buyer. A tree does not get ruined by staying in the ground.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הַאי דְּכִי מְשַׁהֵי לֵהּ פָּסֵיד,
phrases.english: but this one, where if he leaves it he loses out,
phrases.notes: This means the standing grain, which spoils if it is not harvested.

phrases.english: I would say he agrees with רבי יהודה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the ברייתא in Step 16 lists several cases
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The tree case alone would not teach that רבי מאיר is strict even with grain, which spoils if left standing.

steps.title: Why the tree and grain cases are not enough
steps.stepSummary: If the ברייתא had only listed the tree and the grain, we might think רבי יהודה is lenient only where the growth is not noticeable. With fodder, the growth is noticeable, so he might agree with רבי מאיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: If we were only taught these two, we would say רבי יהודה is lenient because their growth is not noticeable. But fodder, whose growth is noticeable, I would say he agrees with רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The second part of the צריכותא. Now the גמרא shows why mentioning fodder (שחת) was also needed, this time for רבי יהודה's side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a tree or grain, any extra growth from staying in the ground is hard to see. So רבי יהודה is not worried. Fodder visibly keeps growing, which tempts the gentile to leave it standing. So we might have thought רבי יהודה would be strict there, like רבי מאיר.

keyTerms.meaning: Two (the two cases, tree and grain)
Fodder: grain cut while still green, used to feed animals

phrases.english: And if it had taught us only these two,
phrases.notes: These are the tree and the standing grain.

phrases.english: [רבי יהודה is lenient] because their growth is not noticeable,
but fodder, whose growth is noticeable —
I would say he agrees with רבי מאיר.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the צריכותא, now explaining the need for the fodder case
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The tree and grain cases alone would not teach that רבי יהודה is lenient even with fodder, whose growth is noticeable.

steps.title: Why the fodder case alone is not enough, so all three are needed
steps.stepSummary: If the ברייתא had only listed fodder, we might think רבי מאיר is strict only there and agrees with רבי יהודה for a tree or grain. So all three cases are necessary.
steps.simpleTranslation: If we were only taught about fodder, we would say רבי מאיר is strict only in that case. But in those other cases, I would say he agrees with רבי יהודה. So all of them are necessary.
steps.whatsHappening: The last part of the צריכותא. The גמרא shows that fodder alone would also be misleading, and then concludes that all three cases had to be stated.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Fodder is the case where the fear is strongest, since its growth is visible. If only fodder were mentioned, we would think רבי מאיר is strict only there. Each case blocks a different mistake, so the ברייתא needs all three.

keyTerms.meaning: Those (the other cases, tree and grain)

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא lists tree, grain, and fodder because each one has a special reason that could have shifted one of the opinions. Listing all three shows that רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה disagree in every case.

phrases.english: And if it had taught us only this one,
phrases.notes: This is the fodder.

phrases.english: only in this case does רבי מאיר say it must be cut first,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל בְּהָנָךְ אֵימָא מוֹדֵי לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה,
phrases.english: but in those cases, I would say he agrees with רבי יהודה,
So it is necessary [to state all three].

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי אַשְׁמְעִינַן בְּהָא, בְּהָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the צריכותא and closes it with 'צריכא'
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: All three cases are needed to show the full extent of the מחלוקת between רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה.

steps.title: Selling an animal on condition it is slaughtered
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים ask: large animals may not normally be sold to a gentile. What is the law if the sale is on condition that he slaughters the animal?
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: an animal sold on condition that it be slaughtered, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question, following the idea of selling 'on condition that he cuts it.' This sets up the discussion that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With trees and grain, רבי יהודה allows a sale on condition that the buyer cuts. The question is whether the same idea works for a large animal. Selling it is normally forbidden because the gentile might use it for work. Could a condition to slaughter it remove that worry?

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked among them (the חכמים)

phrases.english: They asked a question:
An animal sold on condition that it be slaughtered, what is the law?
phrases.notes: Selling large animals to a gentile is normally forbidden, since he might use them for work.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the 'on condition to cut' idea from the ברייתא and asks whether it applies to animals
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does a condition to slaughter allow selling a large animal to a gentile?

steps.title: Why might an animal be different from a tree?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains its question. Maybe רבי יהודה allowed the tree sale because the tree is not in the גוי's control, so he cannot delay cutting it. An animal is in the גוי's control, so he could keep it alive. Or maybe there is no difference.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, what is רבי יהודה's reason for allowing it? Is it because the trees are not in the גוי's domain, so he cannot leave them standing? But an animal stands in the גוי's domain, so he would keep it. Or perhaps there is no difference?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is spelling out both sides of the question it asked in step 20, so we can see why the answer is not obvious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The tree stays on the Jew's land, so the Jew can make the גוי cut it. A bought animal goes home with the גוי, so nobody can make him slaughter it. The question is whether רבי יהודה's allowance depends on that control or applies in every case.

keyTerms.meaning: keeps, delays, leaves as it is
or perhaps there is no difference

phrases.aramaic: הָתָם טַעְמָא מַאי שָׁרֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה?
phrases.english: There, what is the reason Rabbi Yehuda permits?
phrases.notes: "There" means the ברייתא from step 16, about selling a tree or grain on condition that the buyer cuts it.

phrases.english: Because they are not standing in his domain
and he is not able to leave them standing,
but an animal,
since it stands in the domain of the gentile,
he will keep it,
or perhaps there is no difference?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם טַעְמָא מַאי שָׁרֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the two sides of the question asked in step 20.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does רבי יהודה's allowance rest on the item staying in the Jew's control? If it does, would it fail for an animal that goes into the גוי's control?

steps.title: A ברייתא shows רבי יהודה allows the animal sale too
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that רבי יהודה allows selling an animal on condition the buyer slaughters it. רבי מאיר allows selling only an animal that is already slaughtered.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear, as it is taught: an animal may be sold on condition that he slaughters it, and he slaughters it. These are the words of רבי יהודה. רבי מאיר says: one may sell him only a slaughtered animal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that answers the question. רבי יהודה treats the animal the same way as the tree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא states plainly that רבי יהודה allows the animal sale on condition it is slaughtered. So his allowance does not depend on the item staying in the Jew's control, and the answer is "no difference." רבי מאיר is consistent and requires the animal to be slaughtered already, just as he required the produce to be cut already.

keyTerms.meaning: an animal that is already slaughtered

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה allows selling a tree, grain, fodder, or even a large animal on condition that the גוי cuts or slaughters it. רבי מאיר requires it to be cut or slaughtered before the sale.

phrases.english: Come and hear, as it is taught:
An animal may be sold on condition that he slaughter it, and he slaughters it,
These are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.
Rabbi Meir says:
One may sell him only a slaughtered animal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from steps 20 and 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: There is no difference. רבי יהודה allows selling an animal on condition it is slaughtered, and רבי מאיר allows selling only a slaughtered animal.

steps.title: New משנה: renting houses and fields to a גוי
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה begins. One may not rent houses to a גוי in ארץ ישראל, and certainly not fields. It then starts to discuss סוריא.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: One may not rent houses to them in ארץ ישראל, and needless to say not fields. And in סוריא...
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה starts. It moves from selling items to a גוי on to renting him houses and fields.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה rules that houses may not be rented to a גוי in ארץ ישראל. Fields are an even stronger case, so the משנה says "needless to say." The ruling for סוריא continues in the next part of the text.

keyTerms.meaning: needless to say, it is even more obvious
Syria, a land next to ארץ ישראל

phrases.english: MISHNA: One may not rent houses to them
in Eretz Yisrael,
and needless to say, fields,
and in Syria

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין מַשְׂכִּירִין לָהֶם בָּתִּים בְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic, renting property to a גוי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In ארץ ישראל, houses may not be rented to a גוי, and certainly not fields.
